title: Introduce Droplet Shepherd and Guarded SLO Rollback Orchestrator
author: Aisha Kapoor
body: Motivation: production incidents over the last quarter reveal two recurring failure modes: (1) abrupt regional overloads that flip tenant circuits and cause large-scale KV cache evictions and (2) blunt rollbacks of SLO enforcement that either over-throttle or leave services under-protected. This change introduces the 'Droplet Shepherd' orchestrator: a lightweight, tenancy-scoped fallback construct that creates ephemeral 'droplets' (micro-fallback routes) for a subset of traffic and couples them with a guarded SLO rollback mechanism. The shepherd enables graded, observable degradation for tenants and provides an automatic rollback safety net when SLO regressions are detected.
commits: a1b2c3d: core: add droplet shepherd controller and lifecycle API
d4e5f6g: runtime: implement droplet routing and KV-preserve fastpath
h7i8j9k: telemetry: add droplet metrics, SLO delta probes and canary harness
review_conversation: Miguel Santos (reviewer): Nice separation of concerns. Question: how does the droplet handle partial KV state? We need a clear invariant to avoid double-eviction when a route is rejoined.

Aisha Kapoor (author): The shepherd sets a droplet annotation that marks keys as droplet-scoped; eviction_preserve.go records those keys and performs a sticky drain. I added comments and a unit test (integration test covers cross-route rejoin) to validate the invariant.
Claire Nguyen (reviewer): Can we gate this behind a runtime flag for Dedicated customers? Also add telemetry tagging so SRE can filter noisy tenants.

Aisha Kapoor (author): Added a feature flag flags.EnableDropletShepherd and an allowlist for ControlledRolloutTenantIDs. All droplet metrics carry tenant_id and route_cohort tags; updated docs/ops to show how to instrument alerts.
Tomás Alvarez (reviewer): CI failing flake on e2e; suggest adding a backoff to the canary harness to avoid races with KV warmup.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Adjusted canary to poll health with exponential backoff; CI rerun passed. See CI summary below.
testing_notes: Local unit+integration verified. Ran a 2-hour canary in staging with 5 tenants across synthetic spike profiles. Observed 40% reduction in eviction churn compared to baseline and smooth SLO delta detection triggering automatic guarded rollback on one canary tenant (rollback path exercised and validated).
operational_playbook: 1) Enable flags.EnableDropletShepherd in staging via helm values.droplet.yaml. 2) Monitor telemetry/droplet_active_count, telemetry/droplet_slo_delta and slo/regression_alert. 3) If large-scale regressions appear, set flags.DropletGlobalPause=true to stop new droplet creation and rely on gradual rejoin (shepherd will attempt rejoin with backoff). 4) For emergency revert, revert feature flag and redeploy canary image tagged <previous-release>.
release_notes:
- Added Droplet Shepherd: graded, tenancy-scoped ephemeral fallback routes to reduce eviction churn and provide incremental degradation strategies.
- Guarded SLO rollback: automatic rollback trigger when SLO delta exceeds configured thresholds with an observational canary window.
- New metrics: droplet_active_count, droplet_rejoin_attempts, droplet_slo_delta.
- Config flags: flags.EnableDropletShepherd, flags.DropletGlobalPause, flags.ControlledRolloutTenantIDs.
notes_for_release_manager: This is feature-gated; no force rollout. Recommend canary in a single region for 48 hours and watch slo/regression_alert and eviction_churn metrics. Schedule a short maintenance window if enabling for >10 tenants in a region.
post_merge_actions:
- Create Linear task to instrument tenant onboarding docs (ENG-4551).
- Add SRE runbook entry referencing docs/ops/droplet-shepherd.md.
- Toggle feature flag in staging and validate rollback path post-merge.
unique_aspects: The droplet concept focuses on micro-fallbacks that preserve KV affinity and avoid broad circuit flips; the guarded rollback adds an observational canary window to prevent oscillatory SLO toggles.
notes: PR was intentionally conservative on default behavior (disabled by default). The implementation favors observable, reversible changes and includes telemetry-driven safety nets.
